relationship.factor: Uncertain future government regulation on private land
relationship.constraint: Perceived threat to silvopasture adoption through uncertainty about future profits
relationship.note: Expert-elicited implementation constraint, not a measured treatment effect or a decline in governance caused by silvopasture. No effect magnitude or statistical significance is inferred.

context.region: South-central Florida; ranchers from Manatee County
context.practice_as_described: Silvopasture integrates trees and cattle pasture. Respondents assessed adopting this practice relative to conventional cattle ranching; no experimental treatment-control comparison.
context.note: SWOT means strengths, weaknesses, opportunities and threats; AHP means analytic hierarchy process. Three opinion leaders: one research/extension specialist, one large rancher, one small rancher (p6). Quote is research/extension specialist perception, not a population estimate. Table 2 is PDF9, printed193 (earlier staging wrongly called it p11). Factor priority 0.578 is within the three threat factors for this respondent, not an effect size, probability, national governance score or runtime weight. The full factor set and priorities are retained in inventory. p14 explains the proposed mechanism: uncertain future environment/endangered-species/tax rules create uncertain returns and deter investment. Source warns against broad generalization because of small sample. Climate class omitted: no supported project-vocabulary classification. Process: re-extracted under v1.9.4 after full main-paper reading; replaces only the unregistered prior staging version of this ID, never a reviewed register record.

raw_name: uncertain government regulations on private land
justification_quote:
Furthermore, ranchers have to deal with long-term investments if they
switch to sivlopasture. If they perceive that the proﬁts of silvopasture would be un-
certain because of future regulations or policies related to the environment, endan-
gered species or taxes, they are less likely to come forward to invest in
silvopasture. A stable policy environment would further sivlopasture adoption.
